prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse layout of a small room: seating and tables occupy the foreground and middle distance, while the windows, radiators, and walls form the farther boundary. Across the five frames, the wearer turns from the left seating area toward the windows and then rightward along the radiator; nearby chairs, sofas, and tables are roughly 0.5–2 m away, while the walls and windows are about 2–4 m away, with several furnishings partly cut off or mutually occluding one another. It makes relative depth ordering clearer than RGB, including the nearer curved sofa and armchair against the farther television, wall, and windows, but it provides no reliable person-facing or gaze information. The estimates are unreliable around bright windows, object boundaries, and the last frame, where some distant wall and radiator regions appear anomalously bright or smear into nearby surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates scattered object regions across the five frames and can indicate their image-plane positions and occlusions: masks appear on the left in frame 1, around the center-right in frames 2–3, low in frame 4, and on the right in frame 5. With RGB context, these regions correspond mainly to parts of seating, cushions, tabletop items, books, and screens at roughly 0.5–3 m, but the displayed class labels such as person, hotdog, cake, and couch frequently disagree with the visible objects, so object identity and inter-object distance are unreliable. The large person-labelled mask in frame 3 does not clearly correspond to a visible person in RGB and therefore cannot safely establish facing direction, gaze, or reach; most actual furnishings are also left unsegmented. The map does show mask overlap, partial truncation, and changing left-right position as the camera turns, but its sparse and erroneous detections make temporal approach or retreat difficult to distinguish from camera rotation.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely empty, so it provides no dependable body or hand geometry for the room and does not support conclusions about people facing the wearer, looking toward the wearer, or reaching for objects. A single small yellow quadrilateral-like detection appears near the lower-right of frame 5, spatially aligned with a nearby screen or tabletop region rather than a clearly visible human body, at approximately 0.5–1.5 m from the camera. No connected torso, limbs, head, or magenta hand skeleton is present in any frame, and any people that might be partly occluded or outside the view are not localized. Relative to RGB, the map only makes the absence of confident pose detections explicit; the lone detection is likely unreliable and cannot establish motion, orientation, inter-person spacing, or reach across the sequence.
